WARNING.

See warning dated 3rd. March 1933 from British Consulate-
General, San Francisco.

R.S.M.ANDERSON.
ROY ANDERSON.
DAVIS ANDE.SON.
R.S.ANDERSON 2nd.

The subject of the above warning has arrived in Los
Angeles; he has apparently been here for about a month; he
called at this Consulate and claimed to have just arrived at
from China. He stated he was employed in the Chinese Customs,
that he was proceeding on leave, and had been asked to look
up two or three British subjects (ex-officers) in Los Angeles
who had applied for positions in the Chinese Customs. He
appeared very well informed respecting China and did not ask
for anything; he got into touch with many ex-officers of the
British Forces to whom he claimed to have been Captain in the
13th. Batt. of the Black Watch during the War. This has been
proven false. He claimed to have been born in Hong Kong, the
son of a certain Roy Anderson, well known in the Chinese
Customs, but that his father was an American citizen and that
he himself had been educated prior to the War in the Virginia
Military Academy, U.S.A. but preferred his British nationality
and joined the British Forces.

The only actual wrong doing which can be established
against him is that he gave a British officer here a forged
cheque for $2.50 and that he did not pay the salary of a
secretary he employed for ten days to look up addresses in
the local directory. He has stated that he is proceeding to
Seattle, where he intends to sail for China on the 22nd.,
taking with him a contract from the Hearst newspapers as a
correspondent. He also approached a local news agency
stating that he represented Reuters and that Reuter, having
broken with the Associated Press, wishes to establish a new
connection in California; he did not attempt to borrow any
money. Reuter's agents in New York deny all knowledge of
Anderson except that they had received various articles from
him which they had not accepted.

DESCRIPTION. Dark hair, brown eyes, small dark moustache,
round face, stoutish build. Wears rimless pince-nez; accent
undefined, but not British - apparently his idea of a British
accent. Appears to be in early thirties; wears small Black
Watch emblem in lapel and greasy soft brown hat and sometimes
very light grey.

Sent to:- Foreign Office, London.
British Embassy, Washington, D.C.
British Passport Control Officer.
Canadian Legation, Washington, D.C.
Consulates-General. New York, Boston, Chicago,
Philadelphia, New Orleans, San Francisco.
Consulates. Baltimore, Savannah, Galveston, Detroit, Seattle,
St. Louis.

BRITISH CONSULATE,
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA. 15th. April, 1933.

警示。

参见英国驻旧金山总领事馆1933年3月3日的警示。

R.S.M. 安德森。
罗伊·安德森。
戴维斯·安德森（原文拼写为 ANDE.SON）。
R.S. 安德森二世。

上述警示对象已抵达洛杉矶；他显然已在此约一个月；他曾到访本领事馆，声称刚从中国抵达。他称受雇于中国海关，正在休假，并受托在洛杉矶探望两三位曾申请中国海关职位的英国侨民（退役军官）。他似乎对中国情况非常了解，并未索取任何物品；他与许多英军退役军官建立了联系，声称战时曾在黑卫士兵团（Black Watch）第13营担任上尉。此事已被证实为虚假。他声称出生于香港，系中国海关知名人士罗伊·安德森之子，但其父为美国公民，而他本人在战前曾就读于美国弗吉尼亚军事学院，但他更倾向于保留英国国籍，并加入了英军。

目前能确证其实际不当行为之处，仅在于他向当地一名英国军官开具了一张面值2.50美元的伪造支票，以及未支付其雇佣十天以在当地电话簿中查找地址的一名秘书的薪水。他声称将前往西雅图，拟于22日乘船赴华，并随身携带一份来自赫斯特报系（Hearst newspapers）的记者聘约。他还接触了当地一家新闻机构，声称代表路透社，并称路透社因与美联社决裂，希望在加州建立新的合作关系；他并未试图借款。路透社驻纽约代理人否认对安德森有任何了解，仅表示曾收到过其寄来的若干稿件，但均未采纳。

体貌特征：黑发，褐眼，留有黑色小胡须，圆脸，体格较壮。佩戴无框夹鼻眼镜；口音不明，但非英国口音——似乎是他自以为的英国口音。年龄看似三十出头；翻领上佩戴一枚小型黑卫士兵团徽章，头戴油腻的软质棕色帽子，有时也戴极浅灰色的帽子。

发送至：伦敦外交部。
英国驻华盛顿特区大使馆。
英国护照管制官。
英国驻华盛顿特区加拿大公使馆。
各总领事馆：纽约、波士顿、芝加哥、费城、新奥尔良、旧金山。
各领事馆：巴尔的摩、萨凡纳、加尔维斯顿、底特律、西雅图、圣路易斯。

英国驻加利福尼亚州洛杉矶领事馆。1933年4月15日。
